summary.text: Patient 1 was referred at birth with EA/TEF and a ~5 cm long gap, had oesophagostomy/gastrostomy on day three, a ten-day uneventful stay and discharge/follow-up, then transverse-colon replacement at age two. Feed-associated day-four cervical leak was explored/repaired with jejunostomy placement; postoperative-day-28 discharge on jejunal feeds was followed by tube removal four weeks later.

At age three there had been two pneumonia admissions; progressive dysphagia limited diet mostly to semi-solids/liquids. Height 90 cm, weight 11 kg, Z-scores -2.8/-2.5 and BMI 13.6 indicated stunting/undernutrition. Labs and all PedsQL domains are retained; physical 90 was preserved but psychosocial scores reduced. Barium/endoscopy showed distal/lower colo-gastric stricture, reflux and tortuous dilated/redundant graft with rigid scope advancement blocked. Specialty follow-up continues.

Endoscopy found a tight stricture 17 cm from incisors with dilated proximal segment and blocked passage. Gastrostomy and five-day-later discharge preceded three months of outpatient follow-up and transverse-colon replacement at age ten. Enteral feeding started postoperative day three; distension/US collections led to confirmed colo-colic leak treated with laparotomy, washout and diverting colostomy, followed by uneventful recovery and day-12 home discharge.

Current height 145 cm, weight 40 kg, Z-scores 0.1/0.3 and BMI 19 are nutritionally normal. Hb 11.2 is borderline low, albumin 35/ferritin 18 reduced, transferrin 300/B12 210 within reference limits; PedsQL physical 82 and psychosocial scores are retained. He remains largely gastrostomy-fed with failed oral solids. Barium shows proximal stricture reported as 8.12 cm, contrast hold-up, distal dilation and native caustic narrowing; endoscopy cannot advance. Colostomy reversal is planned.
